Both have been held in a detention centre in Brooklyn since January. Their trial is set to begin in June 2027.

events.headline: Thousands to march in Madrid for Maricarmen
events.text: Thousands of people are expected to march through central Madrid this evening, in memory of María del Carmen Abascal. The 87-year-old's eviction from her flat triggered mass protests over Spain's housing crisis. An investment firm had bought the flat, and sought to increase her rent by 230 percent, The Guardian reports. She died in hospital on Wednesday night, a fortnight after the eviction. Her case prompted the government to propose emergency measures for the rental market. When those measures were voted down last week, Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez announced a snap general election.

The army is said to have retaken the strategic city from Tuareg separatists. It would be a major symbolic gain for Mali's military government, which lost the city six months ago.

events.headline: London votes in Holborn and St Pancras
events.text: Londoners are voting in a by-election in Holborn and St Pancras, the seat vacated by former Prime Minister Keir Starmer. The Green Party leader, Zack Polanski, is among the candidates, Al Jazeera reports. Labour has held the seat continuously since its creation in 1983. The vote is seen as a first test of whether Prime Minister Andy Burnham can restore voters' faith in Labour.

events.headline: 180,000 giant tortoises found in Seychelles
events.text: And finally, a survey has found about 180,000 giant tortoises living on Aldabra Atoll, an island in Seychelles. It is the highest figure ever recorded for the species, The Guardian reports. It also far exceeds the human population of Seychelles. In the 19th century, fewer than 1,000 Aldabra tortoises were left on the island. The island became a strict nature reserve in 1981, and a Unesco site in 1982.
